title: Making File Names Unique
statement:
You create one folder per entry of `names`, in order, and folder `i` asks for the name `names[i]`. No two folders may share a name: if the requested name is already taken by an earlier folder, the system instead gives it the name `names[i] + "(" + k + ")"`, using the smallest positive integer `k` for which that name is still free.

Return an array `ans` of the same length where `ans[i]` is the name folder `i` actually received. Every name received counts as taken for later folders, even one produced by adding a suffix.
constraints: names[i] contains only lowercase English letters, digits and the characters '(' and ')'
notes:
## Intuition

The direct method keeps the set of taken names and, for a repeated name, tries `(1)`, `(2)`, `(3)`... until one is free. With many copies of one name that restarts from `(1)` every time and becomes quadratic. The fix is to remember, for each requested name, the suffix where the next search should start: every smaller suffix is already known to be taken.

## Approach

1. Keep a map `nextSuffix`. Its keys are all names taken so far; the value is the smallest `k` that might still be free for that name.
2. For each `name`: if it is not a key, it is free. Take it as is, store `nextSuffix[name] = 1`, and move on.
3. Otherwise start `k` at `nextSuffix[name]` and increase it while `name(k)` is already taken.
4. Take `unique = name(k)`. Store `k + 1` as the next start for `name`, and add `unique` itself as a taken name with start `1`, since it may be requested later.
5. Return `result`.

## Example 1, step by step

`names = ["pes", "fifa", "gta", "pes(2019)"]`. `"pes"`, `"fifa"` and `"gta"` are not in `nextSuffix`, so each is kept unchanged and stored with `1`. `"pes(2019)"` is a different string from `"pes"`, also not a key, so it is kept too. The answer equals the input: `["pes", "fifa", "gta", "pes(2019)"]`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n · L) on average, with L the name length: the suffixes tried for a name only move forward, and each one skipped is a distinct name already taken, so all searches together try O(n) suffixes.
- Space: O(n · L) for the map and the result.

## Pitfalls

- A suffixed name such as `"a(1)"` must be stored as taken; a later request for `"a(1)"` then becomes `"a(1)(1)"`.
- Names already written with a suffix by the user (like `"gta(1)"`) block that suffix, so the search must skip them.
- `k` starts at 1: `"a(0)"` never blocks anything for `"a"`.
- Without remembering `nextSuffix`, 2,000 copies of one name take about 2 million checks.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `nextSuffix` | every taken name, mapped to the first suffix worth trying for it |
| `result` | the names assigned so far, in order |
| `name` | the name requested by the current folder |
| `k` | suffix currently being tried |
| `unique` | the free name `name(k)` that was assigned |

narration.2: Map every taken name to the first suffix number worth trying for it.
narration.3: Collect the names actually assigned, in folder order.
narration.4: Handle the folders in the order they are created.
narration.6: Mark it as taken; a future copy should start trying from suffix 1.
narration.7: A free name is used exactly as requested.
narration.10: The name is taken: resume the search where the last copy of this name stopped.
narration.11: Skip every suffix that is already taken, including ones the user typed in.
narration.14: This is the free name for the folder.
narration.15: The next copy of the same name can start one past this suffix.
narration.16: The new name is now taken too, and a request for it later would start at suffix 1.
narration.17: Record the name this folder received.
narration.19: Every folder has a unique name; return them.
